s1.syndrome_frame: Progressively enlarging, painless, ulcerated skin lesions with blackish crusting in an immunocompromised patient
salient_findings: Painless nodular lesions on the forehead and right cheek
Arborizing telangiectasias and peripheral pigment on dermoscopy
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 70s
Lesions are progressively enlarging
Lesions are painless
No fever, pain, or discharge from the lesions
Patient has a history of kidney transplant in 2004
Patient is immunocompromised
Lesions have central ulceration with hemorrhagic crusting
Dermoscopy shows arborizing telangiectasias, central ulceration with crusting, and peripheral pigment
Histopathological examination shows extensive dermal collection of lymphocytes, histiocytes, and macrophages
Intracellular yeasts with surrounding halos were identified on histopathological examination

raw.syndrome_frame: Progressively enlarging, painless, ulcerated skin lesions with blackish crusting in an immunocompromised patient

shortlist.label: Cryptococcosis
shortlist.why_kept: Immunocompromised patient with progressively enlarging, painless, ulcerated skin lesions and histopathological examination showing intracellular yeasts

shortlist.label: Blastomycosis
shortlist.why_kept: Similar clinical presentation and histopathological findings, including intracellular yeasts with surrounding halos

shortlist.label: Histoplasmosis
shortlist.why_kept: Immunocompromised patient with skin lesions and histopathological examination showing lymphocytes, histiocytes, and macrophages, which could be consistent with histoplasmosis

shortlist.label: Kaposi's sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Immunocompromised patient with skin lesions, which could be consistent with Kaposi's sarcoma, although the histopathological findings are not typical

shortlist.label: Post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder
shortlist.why_kept: Immunocompromised patient with a history of kidney transplant and skin lesions, which could be consistent with post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder

raw.rationale: The presence of intracellular yeasts with surrounding halos on histopathological examination is characteristic of Cryptococcosis, particularly in an immunocompromised patient

rejected.label: Blastomycosis
rejected.why: Blastomycosis typically presents with broad-based budding yeasts, not seen in this case

rejected.label: Histoplasmosis
rejected.why: Histoplasmosis usually presents with smaller yeasts and a different clinical context

rejected.label: Kaposi's sarcoma
rejected.why: Kaposi's sarcoma typically presents with violaceous lesions and a distinct histopathological pattern

rejected.label: Post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with lymphoid proliferation and not with the characteristic yeasts seen in this case
